name: Endotine brow lift

lead: An Endotine brow lift is an endoscopic brow lift that uses an absorbable fixation device with small tines to hold the lifted tissue while it heals. The device was designed as an alternative to screws, sutures or bone tunnels for fixing the forehead [3].

The appearance payoff is a raised brow position that opens the eye area and reduces a tired or heavy look. A one-year comparison of three brow-lift techniques that included Endotine looked at sustainability, noting evidence on durability is sparse [7]. Case and cohort reports describe outcomes and rare complications [2][4][5].

paras: A surgeon makes small scalp incisions, lifts the forehead tissue with an endoscope, and anchors it with the implant, which the body absorbs over time. It is sometimes combined with eyelid surgery.

General risks include numbness, bleeding, infection, asymmetry and hair loss near incisions. A 2024 case report described skull osteolysis 8 years after Endotine fixation [2]. The device may shift early in healing and may not support thick brows or heavy tissue.

angle.text: Patients and surgeons use the technique to raise a low or heavy brow and soften forehead lines. The implant is chosen as a fixation method that dissolves.

lead: The Endotine brow lift is a variant of the endoscopic brow lift in which an absorbable implant with small tines, the Endotine Forehead device, fixes the elevated tissue in its new position [1]. A later version of the device is called Ultratine [2].

A brow lift raises drooping eyebrows and smooths forehead lines; endoscopic approaches through short incisions became the most common technique, replacing coronal incisions [3]. For people seeking a more open eye area, the surgery repositions the brow.

Research on Endotine includes a scoping review of fixation techniques in endoscopic brow lifts, which noted limited comparative data [1], a 36-patient one-year sustainability study [4], and a controlled clinical comparison of the Ultratine device [2].
infobox: Numbness, hair loss, implant movement, rare osteolysis [5]

paras: Endoscopic brow lifts have used cortical tunnels, absorbable devices like Endotine, adhesives and sutures for fixation [1]. Wikipedia notes the endoscopic route is the most commonly used and that Endotine implants may move during early healing and may not support thick forehead tissue [3].

A 2024 case report linked focal skull osteolysis to Endotine fixation eight years after two endoscopic brow lifts, calling for long-term research [5]. In general, endoscopic lifts are most associated with hair loss near incisions and coronal lifts with scalp numbness [3].

A prospective cohort of 10 women with an absorbable Endotine ST midface device reported significant aesthetic improvement in nine at six months [6]. A study of Endotine forehead fixation in endoscopic brow lift was published in 2005 [7]. An Ultratine comparison evaluated the evolved device [2]. A one-year study of 36 patients compared direct browpexy, transpalpebral and Endotine fixation [4]. A 2025 scoping review of 27 papers found heterogeneous complication reporting [1].
